research_question: Hurricanes with more feminine names are perceived as less threatening and hence lead to fewer precautionary measures by the general public.

ivs.description: Continuous masculinity–femininity index for hurricane names (higher = more feminine) rated by independent coders; used as the main predictor of interest.
Binary gender indicator for the hurricane name (0 = male, 1 = female); used as an alternative binary predictor of name femininity.

dv.description: Total number of deaths caused by the hurricane (analysis uses a log(1+alldeaths) transformation as the outcome).

controls.description: Maximum wind speed of the hurricane at landfall (a measure of storm intensity).
Minimum pressure of the hurricane at landfall (a measure of storm intensity).
Estimated property damage normalized to 2015 monetary values (proxy for storm exposure/severity).
Year the hurricane occurred (included to adjust for temporal trends).

extracted_analysis.analysis_code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# Load data

df = pd.read_csv('hurricane.csv')

# Basic cleaning / transformations

df['log_deaths'] = np.log1p(df['alldeaths'])

# Main model: femininity rating with controls for storm intensity and damage
# Controls chosen to approximate storm strength/exposure
model1 = smf.ols('log_deaths ~ masfem + wind + min + ndam15 + year', data=df).fit(cov_type='HC3')

# Alternative model using binary gender indicator
model2 = smf.ols('log_deaths ~ gender_mf + wind + min + ndam15 + year', data=df).fit(cov_type='HC3')

# Simple correlation (no controls)
cor_masfem = df['masfem'].corr(df['log_deaths'])

print('N:', len(df))
print('Correlation masfem vs log_deaths:', cor_masfem)
print('\nModel 1 (masfem):')
print(model1.summary().tables[1])
print('\nModel 2 (gender_mf):')
print(model2.summary().tables[1])

# Save key results to a small dict for downstream use if needed
results = {
    'n': len(df),
    'cor_masfem_log_deaths': float(cor_masfem),
    'model1_masfem_coef': float(model1.params['masfem']),
    'model1_masfem_p': float(model1.pvalues['masfem']),
    'model2_gender_coef': float(model2.params['gender_mf']),
    'model2_gender_p': float(model2.pvalues['gender_mf']),
}

pd.Series(results).to_csv('analysis_results.csv')
